interface_budget-1.reason: Acted in plan v100: section 7 names scripts/spine_benchmark.py --machine, required with --shots and with no default, as replacing the implicit MAST default.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the surface-bearing modules hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces: `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` (`RemoteEddbExtractor`, `SshTransport` behind one batch contract), `imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py` (one converter entry point over the deck/geo.in grammars), and `tokamap_export.export_tokamap_directory` (one public function over the collapse of unit x sign x COCOS into `scale`). The new §7 behaviour is added to these owners, not spread over parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the proposals extend the named owners rather than fork them: store addressing via `StoreEngine.open` + `read_geometry_table` (imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py), pins via `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.resolve_machine_description`, equilibrium scoring via `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py` and `imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py`, and the EQDB store via `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py`. No second resolver, store or scorer is added; no existing grid-writer owner exists for eddb.py to duplicate.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §7 adds a CLI option (`--machine` in `scripts/spine_benchmark.py`) without naming it or stating what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched both named codebases (imas-codex, imas-ambix) and nova, and for every mechanism it names the owner it extends: §2 reuses `imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py` (visible as `_unit_factor`, `_sign_factor`, `export_tokamap_directory`), §3 reuses the FAIR-MAST mirror's non-remote path, §4 extends `StoreEngine.open`/`read_geometry_table`, §5 reuses `load_packaged_signal_map` and `VirtualZarrView`, §6 reuses `score_convention`/`read_level2_observation` etc, §7 extends `RemoteEddbExtractor`, `eddb.py`, `resolve_machine_description` and `judge_geometry`. Every claim was checked by opening the code, not by reading the plan's account of it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no proposal is a passive forwarder. §4's `struct_array_entry` and the store-layout slots are justified in-text as a widening of an existing contract that had no such capability ("retires nothing, because no binding could select a struct-array entry before"; "the engine cannot choose a layout from what it is given today"), and §7's grid writer shares invariants with `write_channel` under the same refuse-to-overwrite rule rather than standing as a second store.
